title: Refactor: Remove redundant err.Error() calls in formatting strings
body:
### Description

In Go, when passing an `error` to formatting functions like `fmt.Errorf` or `logrus.Warnf`, explicitly calling `.Error()` is redundant and generally considered an anti-pattern. The formatting verbs (like `%s`, `%v`, `%q`) automatically invoke the `Error()` method on objects that implement the `error` interface.

There are currently many places in the codebase where `err.Error()` is unnecessarily called inside formatting functions. For example:

```go
// Current
logrus.Warnf("could not release port allocation (%d): %s", newPort, err.Error())

// Proposed
logrus.Warnf("could not release port allocation (%d): %v", newPort, err)
